video.title: Kawhi Leonard Is BACK In Toronto! NBA Blockbuster Trade

summary: Josh Lloyd breaks down a trade that sends Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors. The Clippers get Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, a first-round pick swap and two second-round picks. For fantasy, he sees it as a clean one-for-one swap. Kawhi takes Ingram's high-usage role in Toronto, which costs RJ Barrett the most and Immanuel Quickley somewhat. Ingram slots into Kawhi's spot on the Clippers and should at least repeat last season's numbers. He would still not draft Kawhi in the top two rounds because of his degenerative knee, but moves him up to round three in roto and round four in head-to-head. He calls the trade a win for both teams, with the Clippers starting a constrained rebuild and Toronto becoming a possible top-four team in the East.

rules.text: In a one-for-one positional swap, the fantasy analysis is simple. The incoming player takes over the outgoing player's usage, and teammates' usage moves up or down from there.
rules.quote: It's basically a one-for-one, position for position. You're just tweaking up the usage that Ingram would have been getting

rules.text: When a high-usage player arrives, the players who rely on usage to produce (like Barrett and Quickley) lose the most. Players who don't depend on usage (like Barnes) are less affected.
rules.quote: Scottie Barnes doesn't get by on usage. He doesn't thrive from usage. RJ Barrett does.

rules.text: A good season from a player with a degenerative injury does not remove the risk. Price in the chronic injury risk even after a healthy year.
rules.quote: irrespective of how it played out last season with Kawhi and his health, it doesn't mean that I trust his knee.

rules.text: Repeated surgeries and problems in the same spot make future missed time more likely. Draft those players lower than their per-game value.
rules.quote: all in the same spot over and over and over again, leads you more likely to have problems that it's going to make him miss time.

rules.text: A player who needs a lot of the ball can put up big numbers without being efficient. Don't judge players by raw counting stats alone.
rules.quote: you give someone enough of the ball and enough shots, they can put up numbers. But is it the best thing for the team

rules.text: Don't invest fantasy picks in low-ceiling role players on bad, unsettled teams just because they might start.
rules.quote: we're not interested in investing in these guys. They shouldn't be, and I don't think we should be from a fantasy point of view
